The config file is line based, so a line break in an instance config key

This addresses GHSA-58vc-fxv9-grp7 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>

GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.1598cfaa8479a16cdf0dd94d17fda6690682c30f:
incusd/instance: Only render regular files as templates

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.f96e0af84a98136c3f7e861cbf818b079b4bb6af:
incusd: Bound reads of files supplied by images and backups

metadata.yaml, templates, the OCI config, the NVRAM file and the DHCP
DUID all come from the instance volume and were read whole, so a sparse
file in an image or backup could exhaust the daemon's memory.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 7c91feb48e314b600a625af9ce24dac1bdb0fdf4)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.19c9283adc6cdc75184ab8c775c3bde0bc74a521:
incusd: Only send the snapshots the source offered

A migration target could name snapshots the source never offered, both
on a refresh and for dependent volumes, and the names were used as path
components on the source.

Keep only the requested names that match the source's own snapshots.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 630bd1537b18707298b2cb298244a91057ad6358)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.b619668f169868930f6668ad2a264884ff2c85d0:
incusd: Lock the instance during rebuild

The rebuild operation deleted and re-unpacked the root volume without
holding the instance lock, so a copy refresh sent during the image
unpack could swap a directory for a symlink and have tar write image
entries onto host files as root. A PATCH during a create did the same by
dropping the inherited create lock.

Take the exclusive lock in the rebuild operation and reload under it, and
stop Update from inheriting the create lock.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit a87ea0cc22a066f4874959a1ff11c458cb1d74e6)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.3052b5d67388a2f37da627c5af95cf11abf15849:
incusd/storage: Serialize custom volume content against access

A custom volume's database record was created before its content was
unpacked, and the SFTP, file, mount and rename paths only needed the
record, so a client could open the volume mid-import and plant a symlink
that redirected the remaining tar members onto host files, written as
root.

Hold a per-volume operation lock while the content is put in place, and
wait on it before serving, mounting, renaming or deleting the volume.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 66c8829ccd27a8783ec097d83eb32e162861e321)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.3a5ff37786da214f442435c0ef2033576900f2f9:
incusd/storage: Reject a custom volume refresh that changes content type

A refresh never compared the content type recorded for the target volume
with the incoming one, so a block volume could be refreshed as a
filesystem volume (or the reverse), mixing the two layouts and leaving a
client-controlled root.img that the daemon then opens by path as root.

Compare the content types before any data moves, in both the copy and
migration refresh paths, and before deleting the target's snapshots.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 8269c0a931c58e09efb907b1cfc8ccd801453fea)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.ef9dc701dcfed329c718fb382b6b2a301e494782:
incusd/storage: Match the volume content type on file, SFTP and NBD

The file and SFTP endpoints served any custom volume as a filesystem
volume, exposing a block volume's root.img directory to the client; the
NBD endpoint did the reverse, running qemu-nbd on a filesystem volume's
user-controlled path. A planted symlink then let the client read or
overwrite host files as root.

Reject non-filesystem volumes on file/SFTP and non-block on NBD, and
refuse a block volume disk path that isn't a regular file.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 065c8decfefde8bb6acb0cabe7039fbc03b2d33e)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.82ea0b379028eb59c37aaf2c007178842340b2ba:
incusd: Confine backup and publish walks to the volume

Instance and custom volume backups and image publish walked a volume by
absolute host path and re-resolved each entry in WriteFile, so a
directory swapped for a symlink mid-walk sent the daemon into the host
filesystem and leaked its files into the tarball.

Walk through an os.Root so an escaping symlink isn't followed, and pin
each entry with an O_PATH descriptor checked against the walk's stat
before reading it.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 9a99bb65f31846765dc036a35ed40b0a94fc52d0)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.a882a59ef2a63db8becf5a1daaeebc69db5ae86c:
incusd: Lock the instance during rename

Rename took no operation lock, though the lock is keyed by name, so a
container renamed while its image was still unpacking left the unpack
with no lock under the new name. A client could then plant a symlink
through the file API and have tar write image entries onto host files.

Take an exclusive rename lock, so a busy instance can't be renamed.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit f43caed7528c5ab7f367d5ac25798fd3bada619c)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.8c227e97907e8360230f3f979c8c34eea336c454:
incusd: Restrict image delta base to an owned fingerprint

The delta base name came from the remote simplestreams server and was
mapped to a file under the images directory with no check, so a client
could point xdelta3 at another project's image or, via a traversal name
and a planted symlink, at any host file read as root.

Only offer a delta source that is a SHA-256 the pulling project holds,
and reject a malformed base name in the client library.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 9b0a0e6b4e066ff54f367c70c7607551cd05b5c8)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.356a18f5e5f5527a396be4bafdf3726fc6be3588:
incusd/storage: Validate initial.mode as an octal mode

initial.mode was validated as a decimal integer but parsed as octal when
the mount path is created, so a value like 888 passed validation and
failed the rebuild after it had deleted the volume, leaving a database
record a client could then alias with an ISO volume.

Validate it the way the mount path creation parses it.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 53a42ef4ce16d3ce9c736e11a747a5018b08ec17)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.8b86fe879e442a6e5cba7297f078b4d3cd95cfff:
incusd: Validate the image fingerprint before recording it

The pulled image's fingerprint, taken from the remote server's reply,
was only re-validated after the database record was created, so a
traversal fingerprint survived as a record whose export and delete built
a path from it, reaching any host file as root.

Validate it, and require it to match the requested value, before the
insert.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit d6ad71dee04908e61d7bab16a52e1fe4a53c982f)
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.ac7b6a12c583df70fef09b6955cb72908f183965:
incusd/storage: Resolve bucket backup before export

The bucket backup export handler built the file path from the backup
name in the URL without looking the backup up, so a traversal name
streamed any root-readable host file.

Load the backup from the database first, as the instance and volume
export handlers do.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

(cherry picked from commit 5a998fcae9fe328d74b219913acbd6a434a44962)

with the incoming one, so a block volume could be refreshed as a
filesystem volume (or the reverse), mixing the two layouts and leaving a
client-controlled root.img that the daemon then opens by path as root.

Compare the content types before any data moves, in both the copy and
migration refresh paths, and before deleting the target's snapshots.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.2f83ca2b9ce8cf8f62e8d129684a8e4f32aaee40:
incusd/storage: Match the volume content type on file, SFTP and NBD

The file and SFTP endpoints served any custom volume as a filesystem
volume, exposing a block volume's root.img directory to the client; the
NBD endpoint did the reverse, running qemu-nbd on a filesystem volume's
user-controlled path. A planted symlink then let the client read or
overwrite host files as root.

Reject non-filesystem volumes on file/SFTP and non-block on NBD, and
refuse a block volume disk path that isn't a regular file.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
GHSA-42X8-664J-84W8.5727c8712536003a8cf3209875b9f01f29e7f258:
incusd: Confine backup and publish walks to the volume

Instance and custom volume backups and image publish walked a volume by
absolute host path and re-resolved each entry in WriteFile, so a
directory swapped for a symlink mid-walk sent the daemon into the host
filesystem and leaked its files into the tarball.

Walk through an os.Root so an escaping symlink isn't followed, and pin
each entry with an O_PATH descriptor checked against the walk's stat
before reading it.

This addresses GHSA-42x8-664j-84w8 (CVE pending)

incusd/images: Don't hold the image lock during downloads

long as it likes, holding up that image for every other project. The
transfer now only holds a per-project lock, with the image lock taken
again once the content is verified.

GHSA-3JGX-FPG2-X499.e53cc6a4e5ca9292f031fc41cde91d43ed6993eb:
incusd: Cancel an image download that stops receiving data

The per-fingerprint image lock is held for the whole transfer and the
remote is chosen by the client, so a remote that sends its headers and
then nothing held up that image for every project. A download with no
data for a minute is now cancelled.

GHSA-23FC-GGG4-5R2R.8010f5c07f3c3a632a1ef97d445e9d2b9af06e26:
incusd/forkproxy: Bound what a proxy device holds on the host

UDP sessions were keyed on the client alone and shared between the
listen ports of a device, and nothing capped relayed connections or
sessions, closed received descriptors on a failed relay, or paced the
accept and dial failure paths, which re-fired at once and logged twice
per attempt.

received descriptors on every path, drop the datagram and pause on a
failed UDP dial, pause on a failed accept and rate limit the warnings.

exits once its last SFTP client has gone, so one idle client blocked the
snapshot task for every project. The wait is now bounded and forkfile
is killed when it runs out.

This addresses GHSA-23fc-ggg4-5r2r (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 6f8a29c9d3140e6955a4c8a4eb9c17993188ebcb)
GHSA-23FC-GGG4-5R2R.7792419163e6bb80f1e11b0201f8891692b3b68e:
incusd/endpoints: Let the kernel pick the vsock port

The listener drew ten ports from the 16-bit range and failed the daemon
startup when all were taken, which a guest can arrange as the vsock port
table is shared with containers. A kernel-assigned port comes from the
full 32-bit range.

This addresses GHSA-23fc-ggg4-5r2r (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit c2726622d5956586227c839208e0333a943e3a43)
GHSA-23FC-GGG4-5R2R.7091c763841d2bc4e68a3fece443508a774c2f01:
incusd/instancewriter: Bound the hard link map

Every hard linked file's tar name was kept until the whole volume was
written, so a tree of many deep links cost the daemon gigabytes.

This addresses GHSA-23fc-ggg4-5r2r (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 1dd8816e6a6ae5b7c0a918e35bdf1b76afcdad08)
GHSA-23FC-GGG4-5R2R.e3b7b00a4d5e91cb4665e7073aac9996d78b1703:
incusd/instance/qemu: Bound the VM console log

The ring buffer was drained until a read came back empty, so a guest
writing faster than the daemon reads kept the loop going, and the log

This addresses GHSA-23fc-ggg4-5r2r (CVE pending)

The helper had already been started when the PID file write failed,

GHSA-23FC-GGG4-5R2R.9ace1602402aa14ffe1501f8d915a4198bb5463c:
incusd/forkfile: Don't spin on a closed listener

Once the signal handler closed the listener, Accept returned at once
and the accept loop retried without pause until the last client went
away, burning a CPU for as long as a client kept its connection open.

This addresses GHSA-23fc-ggg4-5r2r (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
GHSA-23FC-GGG4-5R2R.941f4bea8d4a5d984263ee30858c67ab48dbf92b:
incusd: Bound the port forward helper

forknet connect dialed without a timeout and nothing limited how long
the helper could run, so an address the guest leaves unanswered kept a
root process on the host for as long as it liked.

Dial with a timeout and kill the helper after a minute.

This addresses GHSA-23fc-ggg4-5r2r (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
GHSA-23FC-GGG4-5R2R.d6c8ad9edb1bf7d1416cd1c5cbadabf72173f02b:
incusd/forkproxy: Bound what a proxy device holds on the host

UDP sessions were keyed on the client alone and shared between the
listen ports of a device, and nothing capped relayed connections or
sessions, closed received descriptors on a failed relay, or paced the
accept and dial failure paths, which re-fired at once and logged twice
per attempt.

Key sessions per listener, cap connections and sessions, close
received descriptors on every path, drop the datagram and pause on a
failed UDP dial, pause on a failed accept and rate limit the warnings.

This addresses GHSA-23fc-ggg4-5r2r (CVE pending)

incusd/auth/oidc: Don't accept an ID token in place of the access token

An ID token passes the access token verification, and the one sent next
to an opaque access token wasn't bound to it, so a client could pick the
token without the subnet restriction.

GHSA-CP5W-98J2-X2HV.2c35e159f6d4f6428cf13454f36b0e2a29bf1a09:
incusd/auth/oidc: Bind JWT access tokens to the client and a subject

Without a configured audience, any JWT signed by the issuer was accepted,
so a token issued to another client authenticated its bearer, and a
provider-signed JWT with no subject logged in as the empty user.

Require a JWT access token to name our client ID and carry a subject.

GHSA-9M5M-CR24-M367.6e0ef10a323bef94fb1a147fd5c88febdbe74639:
incusd: Reload the trust cache when a project is deleted or renamed

The TLS authorizer matches restricted certificates by project name from
a cache that only certificate changes refreshed, so a certificate kept
its access to a deleted or renamed project's name until something else
reloaded the cache, including a new project created under that name.

GHSA-V855-HXM9-5PWG.75f769f4b24d2d783dbfa17322e3da5430e03722:
incusd: Keep one tenant's snapshots from blocking everyone else's

The scheduled snapshot tasks stopped at the first instance or volume
that failed, matched schedules by searching for the next tick inside the
database transaction, and accepted a snapshots.pattern that can't be
rendered. One tenant could thereby stall or skip other projects'
snapshots. Schedules are now matched in constant time and capped at 64
entries, patterns are validated, and a failure is logged and skipped.

This addresses GHSA-v855-hxm9-5pwg (CVE pending)

incusd/endpoints: Keep accepting on the local socket after a failed accept

A transient accept error such as EMFILE ended the accept loop for good,
so the local socket stayed dead once descriptors were free again.

This addresses GHSA-v855-hxm9-5pwg (CVE pending)

client dropped the connection, and deleting that record removed any
host interface named in bridge.external_interfaces. The revert now

This addresses GHSA-4j59-4pqh-f3qm (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit c029dc9f801df0f350578168f52cd30ba6cacda6)
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.f3adcc6ed94ae3037eaec49bce6bd19754fc0885:
incusd: Remove replaced image volumes only once unreferenced

Refreshing an image deleted the old fingerprint's volume on every
pool without checking other projects, and the auto-update task put
records it had not updated on its delete list, so one project's
refresh broke or removed another project's copy of the same image.

This addresses GHSA-4j59-4pqh-f3qm (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 842f099c0d28a43d0a4c997ca6f9f05921517f94)
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.b34ee24889ea51fd14faf82381618360092b1c66:
incusd: Never replace stored image files on upload

Uploads, publishes and downloads moved their files straight into the
shared image store, so the same bytes split at a different place, or
with an empty rootfs part, replaced another project's copy and broke
it. A stored copy is now kept, a different split is refused, an empty
rootfs part is rejected and a failed import removes what it stored.

This addresses GHSA-4j59-4pqh-f3qm (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit f47d839a2d6783428cd3e70add47a3bda6ff54d3)
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.205933ab657be1f5da36b2470bdfab0b01460150:
incusd: Give image upload tokens their own operation type

A push mode upload token was the same ImageToken operation as a
download secret, so a client allowed to create images could request an
upload token for any fingerprint and use it to export a private image.

This addresses GHSA-4j59-4pqh-f3qm (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit b98ffc583baa94b5c2353e45dbd1ffb3c5639e9f)
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.149ad26e578fe6304737b9a81ad5d22cd4b20d86:
incusd/images: Stream split publish files through the hash

Both files were read into memory to be hashed, so publishing a large
instance in split format cost the daemon the size of its rootfs.

This addresses GHSA-4j59-4pqh-f3qm (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit cfb95f200b1281e1aaf55d6692ecfde52614853d)
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.2241e9c9e2376cbe1f6a34513f28fdcd948fc8f6:
incusd: Store downloaded images under the hash of their content

A remote claiming an OCI image skips the client's fingerprint check,
so a client controlling an image server could store any bytes under a
fingerprint of its choosing and either attach its record to another
project's private image or poison the shared copy before others pull
it. The client now reports the hash it computed and the daemon records
the image under that hash when it differs from the requested one.

This addresses GHSA-4j59-4pqh-f3qm (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 6203810c460ebb04877943683a9edb87c8b3c7ce)
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.92268e03995fa08b5ecbf3a8b36ca334b81c5bf7:
client/oci: Fingerprint the manifest and pin the copy to it

The OCI fingerprint only hashed the layer digests, so images with the
same layers but a different configuration shared a fingerprint, and
the copy re-resolved the tag so a registry could serve the inspected
manifest to one request and other content to the next. The manifest
digest is now part of the fingerprint and the copy is pinned to it.

This addresses GHSA-4j59-4pqh-f3qm (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit d35306905c0a4f7824303638bb4f8088acc42a66)
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.e922a410f7f039be2b0af36b2770b5bd816afd5d:
incusd: Limit image token callers to the raw upload

The token check only gated entry to the handler, so a token holder
could send any JSON request form, minting new tokens for private images
or importing images under its own aliases.

This addresses GHSA-4j59-4pqh-f3qm (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit c6e03b4faf383bbbbd3ec80acdfea2a2869db412)
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.9560d36f8580d144a53996d5ead3fed0e0911d98:
incusd: Only reuse public images from other projects on refresh

Image refresh and auto-update run without a request, which skipped the
view check on reusing another project's image, so a remote alias could
be pointed at a fingerprint prefix to copy any private image. Internal
callers now only reuse public images and download the rest, and the
fingerprint a remote returns must be a full one before any lookup.

A missing image with no server to fetch it from is now an error rather
than a nil dereference.

incusd/images: Expire and bound image tokens

Image tokens held their request metadata in memory forever and a
project could create as many as it liked. They now expire after an
hour, are swept with the other tokens and are capped per project.

GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.f73fbc53367a19365b99ed0476ce1447cbe70d42:
incusd/images: Stream split publish files through the hash

instance in split format cost the daemon the size of its rootfs.

GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.07e1a22c88bce2e486c0e48c7393cb1503e5dc6a:
incusd: Store downloaded images under the hash of their content

A remote claiming an OCI image skips the client's fingerprint check,
so a client controlling an image server could store any bytes under a
fingerprint of its choosing and either attach its record to another
project's private image or poison the shared copy before others pull
it. The client now reports the hash it computed and the daemon records
the image under that hash when it differs from the requested one.

This addresses GHSA-4j59-4pqh-f3qm (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.1f3b2372413d5ecb441c210c500a44f817c2f965:
client/oci: Fingerprint the manifest and pin the copy to it

The OCI fingerprint only hashed the layer digests, so images with the
same layers but a different configuration shared a fingerprint, and
the copy re-resolved the tag so a registry could serve the inspected
manifest to one request and other content to the next. The manifest
digest is now part of the fingerprint and the copy is pinned to it.

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.6714a95bed3647146b72c8a55309c19a6ed7c2bb:
incusd: Remove replaced image volumes only once unreferenced

Refreshing an image deleted the old fingerprint's volume on every
pool without checking other projects, and the auto-update task put
records it had not updated on its delete list, so one project's
refresh broke or removed another project's copy of the same image.

This addresses GHSA-4j59-4pqh-f3qm (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
GHSA-4J59-4PQH-F3QM.418d88e1a2bf6ce1ac279e489b09dcd09e2b766d:
incusd: Never replace stored image files on upload

Uploads, publishes and downloads moved their files straight into the
shared image store, so the same bytes split at a different place, or
with an empty rootfs part, replaced another project's copy and broke
it. A stored copy is now kept, a different split is refused, an empty
rootfs part is rejected and a failed import removes what it stored.

incusd: Validate volatile hardware addresses

volatile.<name>.hwaddr accepted any string and restricted clients may
set it, so a value with line breaks was written as extra dnsmasq
dhcp-host lines on a shared bridge. The last_state keys are no longer
treated as safe for restricted clients either.

GHSA-MMH3-JFJC-6VC2.52b4ea80f3ff63378f5d5d96592ba28c8b243c6d:
incusd: Don't let an image plant a liblxc config file

liblxc loads <lxcpath>/<name>/config and acts on <name>/partial on its
own, and that directory is the instance volume, so an image carrying a
top-level "config" file had it loaded as the container's LXC config,
running its hooks as host root and bypassing the raw.lxc restriction.

and strip them when filling a container volume.

(cherry picked from commit 73d3c6a9788b7af0231802a1dc15d7f658fb0851)
GHSA-MMH3-JFJC-6VC2.b956087ba75c55da831110eb48137791f54befd7:
incusd: Validate the syscall allow and deny lists

The lists were copied verbatim into the seccomp policy, so a line could
carry the notify action and have the daemon handle syscalls it never
asked to intercept.

This addresses GHSA-mmh3-jfjc-6vc2 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 93d328882aea0e9023545491e0d70d93f9037b5f)
GHSA-MMH3-JFJC-6VC2.2e46cc24dbffaada92aa64dd504ce539543df2cc:
incusd: Serialize instance rewrites on volume rename and profile update

Rewriting the instances affected by a custom volume rename/move or a
profile update wrote back a copy of each instance record listed before
the loop, without the instance lock or a reload, so a concurrent
instance update could be silently reverted, dropping a required key like
security.idmap.isolated. The volume path also ran the write inside the
listing transaction, holding the global database connection for 30s.

Collect the instances first, then update each under its operation lock
from the current record, and refresh the profile-update path the same
way.

This addresses GHSA-mmh3-jfjc-6vc2 (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit ebcdbdc2fea983f2a536351a32c3139853038b8c)
GHSA-MMH3-JFJC-6VC2.2eda10be3dbdf20d436a41535b3bb401994e9507:
incusd/project: Fail closed when the checked profile or instance is gone

The profile and instance update restriction checks looked the object up
by name in a freshly fetched project and had no not-found branch. A
client could rename a profile away and back around its update to skip
the check and store raw.lxc, and a rename during a snapshot restore
crashed the daemon on a nil dereference.

Return not-found when the object isn't there, and re-check the profile
in the transaction that writes it.

GHSA-P8FX-6XXM-25WH.87d014f467bc92f4f93f531747b449fe8ffbd4b2:
incusd: Keep instance volume directories root-owned on receive

The instance directory is the only thing keeping local users out of a
container's setuid files, but rsync, image unpack and backup unpack all
applied the owner the incoming stream stated for the transfer root to
that directory, letting the sender take ownership of it.

Restore the directory's owner after an rsync receive, mount the receive
nosuid/nodev, and reset the owner to root after image and backup unpack.

This addresses GHSA-p8fx-6xxm-25wh (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 890694fdb0c0cf0a94854465228d1a2813e89c19)
GHSA-P8FX-6XXM-25WH.35e3a12fbc54c5b319aee3a4e46a2f61f1ac161a:
incusd/device: Mount disk staging bind mounts nosuid

A disk device's source is bind-mounted under a traversable devices
directory while a container starts. The mount kept setuid bits, so a
local user who knew the path could run a setuid-root file from their own
custom volume as root during the start window.

Set nosuid on the staging mount.

This addresses GHSA-p8fx-6xxm-25wh (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit a0e857c6a844826cedb86630c70c83b0fd7ae151)
GHSA-P8FX-6XXM-25WH.8d92cbbf614cc7585c4909afe4b2978c46b4406a:
incusd: Harden forkproxy unix socket handling

The forkproxy child chowned and chmodded the listen socket by path after
binding, so a local user owning the directory could swap it for a
symlink and have root chown an arbitrary host file. The AppArmor profile
also resolved both socket paths on the host and printed them unquoted,
letting a planted symlink inject policy or block the start.

Bind with the final mode, chown the socket through an O_NOFOLLOW
descriptor, resolve only the host-side path (just the directory for a
host listen socket), quote the rules and reject metacharacters.

This addresses GHSA-p8fx-6xxm-25wh (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit fe31a597a0d5b1b49a16564ba67a5c070d5d83d6)
GHSA-P8FX-6XXM-25WH.a9f3680cf08ce7b7372736650f744eec4fbd3033:
incusd/rsync: Only accept the rsync helper on the transfer socket

The sending side listened on an abstract unix socket and handed the
first connection to the transfer. Any local user could connect first,
read the whole tree and feed the receiving root rsync setuid files.

Accept only a peer running as our own effective user, and keep the
listener open until it connects. Same change in the migration tools.

This addresses GHSA-p8fx-6xxm-25wh (CVE pending)

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>
(cherry picked from commit 3f8392d5c5dd667ae91b59bf319f5eb023c85022)

GHSA-F5F6-6X9Q-GH3F.e3ea72d9be9977f015a0515f4eb07b2cbfa524fc:
incusd/storage: Reject rootfs content in a split image metadata tarball

A split image is unpacked in two runs: the metadata tarball into the
volume, then the rootfs archive into the rootfs directory. The metadata
tarball could carry its own rootfs/ members, leaving a symlink there
that redirected the second run's writes onto host files as root.

Refuse a non-empty rootfs directory before the rootfs archive is
unpacked into it.

GHSA-3C9P-936J-GV99.ca0edc34b58832734fe28ae58e8f64f6957547e2:
incusd/auth/tls: Only inherit default project objects through a project using them

All-projects listings granted restricted certificates read access to
every image, profile, volume, bucket, network and zone in the default
project, regardless of whether any of the certificate's projects
inherits that type of object from it. A restricted client with no
project, or with a project that has the matching feature enabled,
could still list the default project's objects, including full
profile configuration.

The single object check and project scoped filtering had the same gap,
admitting default project objects through any trusted project, so a
restricted client could copy a default volume or reuse a private
default image from a project holding its own.

Give the TLS driver access to project configuration and only admit
default project objects when the relevant certificate project relies
on the default project for that type.

This addresses GHSA-3c9p-936j-gv99 (CVE pending)

(cherry picked from commit d9efcf80787483a40b684ebe700ac779819dc2fe)

GHSA-7643-2VQQ-56P3.7f249375baee745a06b239eca87fb43ef28968ab:
incusd: Check certificate ownership on every non-admin update

Non-admin clients may update their own trust entry, but the check that
the requesting certificate is the one being updated only ran when the
certificate material was replaced. A description-only update skipped it,
so any trusted client could rewrite the description of another trust
entry from its fingerprint.

Always verify the caller holds the target certificate before applying a
non-admin update.

This addresses GHSA-7643-2vqq-56p3 (CVE pending)

GHSA-H2J8-4CRH-VHFC.f713b5d57b6857c662371f398f9450f2c8f6f64d:
incusd/operations: Keep websocket secrets out of events and queries

Migration operations embed their per-connection websocket secrets in the
operation metadata, which was broadcast to every event listener and
returned by operation queries. Unlike exec and console, the migration
websocket authorizes on the secret alone, so a project event viewer could
read the secret and hijack an in-flight migration's data channels.

Return the connection secrets only in the synchronous create response and
strip them from every other render. The client keeps the create-response
secrets across later operation updates so push clients still find them.

This addresses GHSA-h2j8-4crh-vhfc (CVE pending)

GHSA-XG75-XF37-CPH9.1031796be7728d36ce9b59bdb3312e48c2cb4aed:
incusd: Only trust the key-proven client certificate

The HTTPS listener uses tls.RequestClientCert, so the TLS handshake only
proves possession of the first certificate in the client's chain. The
authentication and certificate ownership checks looped over the whole
chain and matched each certificate against the trust store, letting a
client authenticate as, or take over, any trust entry by appending that
entry's public certificate to its own chain.

Match only the first peer certificate in every trust-store check.

This addresses GHSA-xg75-xf37-cph9 (CVE pending)

GHSA-P45F-GQQJ-6QQ3.18de390da967f4d928b6a7dea67aa8179a379067:
incusd/storage: Validate snapshot names from the backup index on import

The snapshot names listed at the top of the backup index are validated
on import, but the database records are created from the names in the
volume config section of the same index, which weren't. A crafted
backup could therefore store a snapshot name containing path traversal
which is later resolved by the storage driver, for example when the
volume is deleted.

GHSA-CWG9-8MC4-HF7J.c3d99b1cb96c76b809a18bd9f8ac7b7ab268d6de:
incusd/operations: Protect token operations from events and cancellation

Token operations are only readable by clients allowed to create the
matching token, but their events, including the secret, were sent to
any client able to view events in the default project. Such a client
could then reconstruct a certificate token and enroll an unrestricted
certificate.

Cancelling an operation also skipped all checks when the operation type
has no associated permission, which includes token operations, so any
authenticated client could cancel them by UUID.

Keep the metadata of token operations out of the event stream and
check access before cancelling an operation. Operations without a
specific permission can be cancelled by their requestor or by clients
able to edit the project.

This addresses GHSA-cwg9-8mc4-hf7j (CVE pending)

GHSA-8R3H-VC36-6XPX.ecccdd82716b899882e67ec17e7a81b23171ed55:
incusd/auth/tls: Restrict inherited reads to the certificate's projects

Restricted certificates get read-only access to resources in the
default project so that projects without a feature enabled can use the
inherited resources. That access was granted regardless of the project
being accessed, so a restricted client could read profiles, images,
volumes, buckets, networks, zones and their backups in the default
project by requesting it directly.

Only allow inherited reads when the request is made through a project
the certificate is trusted for. Additionally hide network zone peer
keys from clients who can't edit the zone, as is done for networks.

This addresses GHSA-8r3h-vc36-6xpx (CVE pending)

GHSA-Q9FC-P923-6VP7.d3cb699621e999f9c9be91296b0715a5bf5c3390:
incusd/storage: Validate dependent volumes received through migration

The names of dependent volumes received through migration were used as
path segments without validation, letting a malicious source create
volumes outside of the storage pool.

The index header sent by the source was also indexed by the position of
the volume in the offer header, with no check that the lists match, and
optional protobuf fields were dereferenced unconditionally, letting a
malicious source crash the daemon.

Validate the names as is done for backups, check the index header
before using it and use the nil-safe protobuf getters.

GHSA-8MGX-H4V8-XQV2.43e6bdeb7530768c3bc2ae0feb2541e48fa365c3:
incusd/storage/s3: Verify signed payloads without buffering

Requests with a signed payload had their whole body read into memory to
verify its hash before the signature was checked and before the
credential role was enforced. Anyone knowing a valid access key could
have the daemon buffer arbitrarily large bodies.

Verify the signature first, using the hash claimed in the request, then
verify the body against that hash as it's consumed. This also stops
buffering objects uploaded by valid credentials. The multipart
completion body is additionally bounded.

CVE-2026-40243.520728f48ad7f083961ac8fba1ecdab96c6c6498:
incusd/network/ovn: Fix TLS validation logic

All 4 of the OVN connection handlers (NB, SB, IC-NB, IC-SB) were using a
rather broken validation logic which would effectively treat any remote
certificate as valid.

The updated logic now correctly uses the configured CA as the only valid
TLS root certificate and then loads the provided remote certificate and
intermediates before validating that a path exists between the root CA
and the server certificate.

Custom logic is used as OVN certificates and connection URLs don't
typically contain valid server name information.

This addresses CVE-2026-40243

CVE-2026-23954.243f9e5fdf78be190e6dd80018392e78c0896159:
incusd/instance/lxc: Restrict path of template files and targets

This fixes three security issues related to file templates:

 - The template target path could be made to be relative or gothrough
   symlinks in a way that could lead to arbitrary write to the host
   filesystem.

 - The template directory could be relative, allowing for arbitrary read
   from the host filesystem.

 - The template file itself could be made relative, allowing for
   arbitrary reads from the host filesystem.

In the case of the template target path, the new logic makes use of the
kernel's openat2 system call which brings a variety of flags that can be
used to restrict path resolution and detect potential issues.

For the template path itself, we now validate that it is a simple local
file and that the template directory isn't a symlink.

This fixes CVE-2026-23954

CVE-2024-6156.349ba03afdf5568355e7529dcc3fd4893272c78f:
incusd/daemon: Skip non-PKI issued trusted certificates when in PKI mode

This addresses LXD CVE-2024-6156 which describes a PKI restriction
bypass when a user with a previously trusted certificate attempts to
interact with Incus following the switch of Incus into PKI mode.

We consider this a very low risk issue as to be affected a system would
need to have been switched to PKI mode AFTER already having trusted
specific clients, having the administrator not performed any cleanup of
the trust store while doing the switch to PKI mode and the previously
trusted client certificate still being in use on a system which
shouldn't be trusted.

Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@stgraber.org>

CVE-2016-1582.f10e1bc47c1b385b396a35e540cb8cd9435783ea:
CVE-2016-1582: Bad permissions after remap

When switching an unprivileged container into privileged mode, the
container directory remains owned by the container uid/gid and has a 755
directory mode rather than the expected 700.

This allows traversal by a host user to reach potentially now
root-owned setuid paths.

Reported-by: Robie Basak
Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@ubuntu.com>

CVE-2016-1581.7e8afe809284da64277eb080b456ab24ea53b516:
CVE-2016-1581: Fix bad permissions on zfs.img

When using a file backed zpool as created by "lxd init", the created
file was world readable, which would allow an untrusted user to read
container data.

This fix makes sure that zfs.img is always created 600 from now on and
also fixes the permission of any zfs.img file at LXD startup time.

Reported-by: Robie Basak
Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@ubuntu.com>

CVE-2015-1340.19c6961cc1012c8a529f20807328a9357f5034f4:
CVE-2015-1340: Fix race condition between fchown and chmod in idmapset

Shifting a container filesystem in an environment where a user can
modify the container's filesystem as it's being shifted (for example if
the LXD server's / was shared over the network) would allow them to make
use of a race (TOCTOU) between the chown and chmod operations, allowing
for an arbitrary path to be chmod-ed rather than the planned container
path.

The fix is to use a file descriptor to the entry being processed,
validate that the entry itself is sane and then interact with the fd.

This is CVE-2015-1340

Reported-by: Seth Arnold
Signed-off-by: Stéphane Graber <stgraber@ubuntu.com>
